The concept of a meme is the relatability to the audience, and its recognizability.

Rather than creating a new image format, using one that already exists and re-purposing it while maintaining its relation to the audience, and the ability for the audience to recognize it as a meme they have seen before and will see again.

Check out KnowYourMeme.org to see a vast variety of memes, and the descriptions of what makes them interesting. Not all memes are interesting to everyone, so learning which have the biggest appeal is what you want to study.
Thanks, I'll check it out. Right now I'm just trying to figure out how to put stuff together.

Make the font ARIAL and in ALL CAPS, Usually people use WHITE with a black border 1-5px width and softened (slightly antialiased to soften it). I use INKSCAPE for my memes and the workflow is the same

1) import image

2) use text tool and then using all caps type out or paste text

3) move and size the text over the meme, and then make it Arial, caps, white ('fill'), black border ('stroke'), smooth 0.2, and 0.8-1.2 width for the stroke properties

4) Then I copy the text and then paste, change the fill to black, and then select it, and hit pagedown to make move it to a layer underneath the white text. Then i move it so it's a 'shadow'. You can also up the 'smooth' and opacity / transparency of the shadow if you want

5) Repeat above steps for other text as applicable (top of meme, bottom of meme text)

6) export as PNG. I usually do 1920 x 1080 (HD), and so I use the lesser dimension to fill the screen (if it's taller than it is wide, I set the height at 1080 and let the width be whatever; if it's wider than it is tall then I make the width be 1920 and the height be whatever...its so it fills the screen one dimension or the other but isn't bigger so that people can see the whole thing in HD)

7) in gimp i open the pNG file and then immediately export it as JPG with 88 quality; floating point oversampling, etc. Adjusting the image as necessary just before this export (like cutting excess, adjusting contrast, sharpness)

8) Then I upload to IMGUR.COM or some other host. THIS IS KEY: after it's uploaded, right click on it and "open image in new tab", and then switch to the new tab, copy THAT URL (the direct url to the image) and then paste THAT into voat and you'll get the image. YOu only want to link to a gallery if you have multiple images.

If you intend on carrying concealed you have two choices with two more sub-choices if that makes sense. Compact size (glock 19 size) or sub-compact size (glock 43 or 26 size). You are not limited to Glock. Many reputable companies produce a quality and for some better products of similar size and type.

Compact is bigger and easier to shoot, recoil is more manageable, and has in double stack configuration 13-15 rounds on average. It is harder to conceal for most people and can become bothersome if you're out on your feet all day.

Sub-compact are a dream to carry, especially in the summer. Easily concealable and you can have it on all day and forget you're carrying with a good holster. Harder to shoot more accurately, more recoil is absorbed by the shooter's hand. Limited ammo capacity.

A single stack configuration of either is alot easier to conceal and easier on your body since they are slimmer.
